blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — HFrEF beta-blocker initiation during hospitalization
stem: A client hospitalized with acute decompensated HFrEF is being considered for initiation of an evidence-based beta-blocker. Which plan is most appropriate?

options.A: Begin a low dose after the client is clinically stabilized and no longer requires IV inotropic therapy; initiation before discharge is appropriate when tolerated.
options.B: Begin the target maintenance dose while the client remains hemodynamically unstable and requires IV inotropic support so therapeutic benefit is achieved sooner.
options.C: Defer beta-blocker initiation until several weeks after discharge even when the client becomes clinically stable in the hospital and no longer needs IV inotropes.
options.D: Withhold evidence-based beta-blocker therapy because a recent HFrEF decompensation makes beta-blockade inappropriate even after clinical stabilization.

rationale: The current AHA/ACC/HFSA heart-failure guideline recommends evidence-based beta-blockers for HFrEF, states that beta-blockers should be initiated at low doses, and notes that they can be safely initiated before hospital discharge when the patient is clinically stabilized and does not require intravenous inotropic therapy for heart failure. Therefore A is the best answer. B initiates therapy during ongoing hemodynamic instability and IV inotropic support and starts at a target rather than low dose. C unnecessarily postpones guideline-supported in-hospital initiation after stabilization. D incorrectly treats a recent decompensation as a continuing contraindication after the client has stabilized.
educational_objective: Initiate an evidence-based HFrEF beta-blocker at a low dose after clinical stabilization and when IV inotropic support is no longer required; appropriate clients may begin therapy before hospital discharge.
source_organization: American Heart Association (AHA), American College of Cardiology (ACC), and Heart Failure Society of America (HFSA)
source_document_title: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
source_version_date: Published April 1, 2022; current AHA guideline resource accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: §7.3.2 Beta Blockers: beta blockers should be initiated at low doses; data show they can be safely initiated before hospital discharge provided patients are clinically stabilized and do not require intravenous inotropic therapy for heart failure. AHA Professional Heart Daily continues to list the 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA guideline as the current heart-failure guideline resource.
source_claim_supported: Evidence-based beta-blockers for HFrEF should be started at low doses and may be initiated before discharge after clinical stabilization when IV inotropic therapy is no longer required.
blueprint_locator: Printed p. 38, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: review pertinent medication data; administer medications safely; educate clients about medications; evaluate therapeutic response and adverse effects; recognize contraindications and precautions.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four options as parallel treatment plans of comparable length and removed isolated never/all/only wording.
Added the guideline-supported low-dose initiation principle to the correct option while keeping the distractors clinically plausible.
Preserved the key stabilization and IV-inotrope criteria without introducing a fixed timing interval unsupported by the guideline.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely combines the guideline-supported prerequisites: clinical stabilization, no IV inotropic requirement, and low-dose initiation. B conflicts with both stabilization and dosing principles, C unnecessarily delays appropriate therapy, and D incorrectly extends the acute decompensation state after stabilization. No second defensible answer or material cueing remains.
